summary: Repaired the exact rejected defect: cmd_recover_stale (default and --owner-confirm), cmd_owner_review_recover --apply, and cmd_release_launch's 'blocked' bucket were persisting a top-level status=blocked (or, for the two owner-gated/apply paths, status=pending/unclaimed -- a forbidden automatic requeue). All four sites now unconditionally persist status=review, worker_status=review_ready, terminal_outcome/review_outcome=process_lost|blocked|validation_failed|scope_rejected|launch_failed|timed_out|cancelled, and enqueue exactly one callback. blocked is a review_outcome value only, never the canonical status, for any claimed-task terminal case. AITools/taskdb.py: added process_lost/stale to _CALLBACK_TRANSITION_MAP (blocked bucket) and widened _task_still_in_matching_terminal_state's blocked branch to accept status in (review, blocked) so the new review-routed blocked-outcome callbacks still deliver, while a genuinely manually-authored blocked card (never claimed) still matches too. Only cmd_reject_review may move a claimed task back to pending -- verified directly for every automated path.
prior_attempt_rejection_reason: recover-stale --owner-confirm and owner-review-recover --apply routed a claimed task straight to pending/unclaimed (forbidden automatic requeue); cmd_recover_stale (default) and cmd_release_launch's blocked bucket persisted a top-level status=blocked instead of status=review (forbidden -- blocked is an outcome value only). The prior attempt also declared PASS with 135 passed / 11 failed and attributed the 11 failures to the environment.
